messages:
ana: quick q — bench smoke-run for model `m-ark-v2` returned a `kv-mismatch` flag. should onboarding fail the ingest, or let the model through with a degraded runtime fallback? we tripped on this in prod last week and would like to avoid surprise rollouts.

mike: my vote is fail-fast for the default path. if the model can't honor the KV cache contract we risk huge latency regressions. but allow an opt-in 'degraded' mode that forces pinning to single-shard runtime + disabled prefix cache.

sam: agreed on fail-fast. we should also classify mismatch severity — e.g., minor signature differences (tensor order) vs full KV layout mismatch. minor => can auto-correct shim; major => block.

jess: want to add a lightweight perf delta check too. sometimes kv layout is fine but latency jumps due to kernel selection. proposal: add a micro-benchmark in ingest that runs 20 token steps + measures p50/p95 on a small GPU instance. If p95 > baseline * 1.4 => block.

ana: @jess typo — that's ana :) but +1. also need a clear UX for model owners: why blocked, which check failed, and remediation steps.

mike: remediation suggestions: 1) link to a converter CLI output (diff of kv layout), 2) recommended quant/compile settings, 3) a quick local repro command. e.g.:
```
./smoke_run --model $MODEL_ID --mode reproduce --samples 20 --save-artifacts ./artifacts/$MODEL_ID
```

sam: ingest-bot should include the exact failing assertion and a small diff snippet. example: `expected kv.shape=(B, N, H) got (B, H, N)` — that immediate hint saves a lot of back-and-forth.

ingest-bot: automated-checks: smoke-run v2 results for m-ark-v2:
- kv-check: FAIL (signature_mismatch)
- micro-perf: WARN (p95 = 1.6x baseline)
- export-valid: PASS
- golden-outputs: PASS (99.1% similarity)

ingest-bot: uploaded artifacts: https://internal.redwood/smoke/artifacts/3123456789/m-ark-v2.zip

jess: for the degraded path we discussed earlier — we should gate it behind a feature flag + require an explicit owner approval in console before allowing the model to serve to traffic. no silent degenerates.

ana: decision proposal (RFC follow-up):
- default: fail onboarding on any kv-check FAIL or micro-perf p95>1.3x baseline
- exception path: allow 'degraded-serving' tag only after manual approval; enforce reduced qps and single-az placement.
- onboarding UI: show failing assertion, artifacts link, and one-click open a ticket to infra/serving with prefilled repro command.

mike: +1. operational note: add a periodic re-eval job to run the micro-benchmark on canary after 24h; if the perf delta persists, auto-disable the degraded flag and alert the owner.

sam: one more thing — add a small compatibility matrix check in registry metadata: declared cache-contract version, tensor-order hint, and preferred kernel flags. If metadata missing, treat as risky and block.

jess: I'll stub a tiny UI mock and the feature-flag flow. ana can you take the RFC follow-up doc + owners? I'll post mock screenshot in #design later.

ana: taking RFC follow-up. I'll draft the doc with explicit signals, thresholds, and example repro flows. tagging owners: mike (runtime), sam (ingest), jess (console). please ack if you want different thresholds.

mike: ack. sam: ack. jess: ack.

ana: thanks — will put the draft in google drive and ping for a 30m sync tomorrow.

mike: small offline note: add a metric for "onboard-block-rate by reason" so PM can see where models are failing (kv vs perf vs export).

sam: good call. ingest-bot can emit those metrics as tags on the checks event.

jess: ok closing here, will share mocks. :sparkles:
